Alex (CEO): quick follow-up to today's all-hands Q&A  drop short strategy/positioning questions here.
Jordan (Growth): what is the one line we should use for customers who compare us to big cloud endpoints?
Alex (CEO): "Redwood: production-first inference that makes latency, cost, and deployment choices predictable." keep it pithy.
Maya (Head of Product): Add a demo line: "See token-level cost, automatic fallbacks, and seamless model pinning in Console."
Ravi (CTO): Tech lede for SEs: we handle runtime complexity (KV caches, batching, quantization variants) so teams avoid building inference plumbing.
Sam (VP Eng): Competitor nuance: if pressed about scale vs hyperscalers, what do we say?
Alex (CEO): Be honest: hyperscalers have global infra; we win on inference economics, developer velocity, and predictable SLAs across hosted/dedicated/private.
Jordan (Growth): For sales decks, can we call out a concrete customer outcome vs self-hosting?
Maya (Head of Product): Example: "Reduced inference unit cost by X% and cut deployment time from months to days in pilot." Use anonymized numbers from case studies.
Sam (VP Eng): Roadmap ask: customers want clearer guidance on when to move to Dedicated. Any timeline?
Maya (Head of Product): Publishing a migration playbook and SLA FAQ in 2 weeks. Also releasing Console cost widgets in the next release.
Ravi (CTO): Note: Dedicated adds reserved GPU pools and routing controls; Private adds VPC + KMS. API stays the same.
Jordan (Growth): Pricing signal: embedding-heavy customers asking for a different model. Any update?
Alex (CEO): We're testing a compute/storage split for embeddings and pilot discounts; no changes for existing customers without opt-in.
allhands-bot: Reminder: fill out the post-all-hands survey in #announcements.
Alex (CEO): thanks everyone  if anything missed, ping the relevant owner and we'll follow up.
